reviews.title: Literally broke my piano because of how frustrating this app is
reviews.text:
TLDR: This app is full of ads, is somehow worse than the web version, is incredibly unintuitive and slow to operate that it made me so mad to the point that I broke my piano

I genuinely cannot believe how bad this app is. And there is no competition for the app so I can’t just switch to anything else. 

First of all, there is a pay wall on everything. Want to play some music then you have to pay 200 bucks a year to get to it. 

Second of all, the app is so unintuitive and unresponsive that it makes actually getting to the music a huge task. Why can’t it just be a click away like the web version. 

And that brings me to my third complaint WHY IS THE WEB VERSION BETTER THAN THE APP???. You have so much more capability and access on the web version of MuseScore. The layout isn’t terrible, it’s somehow faster and easier to use than the app, and it lessens the paywalls on everything. I was literally going to pay 8$ to buy a piece of sheet music on the app but when I switched to the web version only cost 1$????. Like how does it make any sense for it to be cheaper to go on the web version and buy it rather than on the app?. Why can’t they just make the app the same as the web version they already have the recipe for a great app JUST IMPLEMENT IT. 

And finally, when your on the app they shove so many premium things on there it just messes up the whole practice flow. I try to click the settings and it opens up the ai practice mode. And I am not paying for that so I try to close it

3/5 app

reviews.title: Very misleading and scammy
reviews.text:
I feel like this is misleading advertising. I downloaded the app specifically because it offered a 7-day free trial, including a 7-day Pro trial. I always cancel free trials immediately so I don’t forget and accidentally get charged. If I like the app, I can always go back and renew the subscription.

However, as soon as I canceled, I immediately lost access to all of the Pro features—even though the app says my trial continues until October 5th. Today is only September 28th.

If canceling the subscription means losing access to the trial immediately, then I don’t understand how this can be advertised as a 7-day free trial. I should be able to use the advertised trial period to actually decide whether I want to pay for the Pro version.

What also concerns me is the pricing structure. From what I’m seeing, you pay for the basic app, then you pay for Pro, and then you’re still expected to pay separately for individual features or items within the app. There are also a large number of 1-star reviews from people complaining about the customer service and feeling that they were repeatedly charged or pressured to purchase additional things.

With so many negative reviews describing similar concerns, I honestly have a hard time understanding how the app has a 4.6-star rating. The number of complaints makes me question how representative that rating really is.

And whatever you do, do not purchase through their website. I’ve seen numerous complaints about how difficult it is to cance

reviews.title: some things about this app
reviews.text:
I had a very frustrating experience with this app. My child purchased a piece of sheet music listed at $0.99, but I was charged twice for it. A 7-day trial for a quarterly subscription was also pre-selected during checkout, which resulted in an additional charge. After disputing it, I still ended up paying about $17 for one piece of music that was supposed to cost $0.99.

What bothers me even more is that the subscription option seems to be pre-selected with purchases, and canceling the subscription is unnecessarily complicated.

The membership also doesn’t seem like a good value. If I buy about 12 pieces a year, the membership fee plus the discounted sheet music actually costs more than simply buying them individually at full price. I’ve also found the same sheet music $2–$3 cheaper on other apps.

Because of the confusing checkout process, poor value, and higher prices, I can’t recommend this app.

Well, the app does let you transpose, but only if you have Musescore PRO+. ($8.33/month) That is insane. I’d rather go through the pain of mentally transposing and writing out an entire new piece of sheet music than pay 8.33 dollars a month to change the key on four pieces. And don’t get me started on the price to buy an individual score. I love Musescore, but that is too much to pay for a single key change. If someone wants to enlighten me and let me know why I need to pay this much for such a small service, please do. I’m open to changing my mind, but for now I am very dissatisfied with this app.

reviews.title: Great concept, not user friendly
reviews.text:
This app has so much potential to be great based on concept alone. Music is such an incredibly important part of so many people’s lives and having access to lessons and scores of user generated music is so awesome. There are so many cool features in the app like the ability to scan in your own sheet music and overall just the convenience of the whole package is great.
Despite all this, I still gave the app one star; this is because of the predatory money making strategies on the app. While it is true that you can listen to previews of sheet music for free, the entire time it will ask you to buy the score every 5 seconds. I understand that this is not entirely the fault of the developers as users set pricing for their own published sheet music, but it is still incredibly annoying. Additionally, the many different plans of access are unclear. There were a few times when I had thought i had purchased one thing but did not gain full access to what I wanted.
Finally I wanted to touch on the subscription model used for pro accounts on the app. The app saves your payment details and will automatically subscribe after a free trial ends. I understand that there are disclaimers for this however, I received no notification in app that I was being automatically signed up for three months of a subscription tier I did not want. Additionally, the subscriptions are priced pretty high for what they really provide. The pro tier only includes one free lesson and a 40% discount on buying scores

reviews.title: Probably the best option but It is terrible IMO
reviews.text:
This app / website has a lot of useful functionality but its subscription model makes it the most annoying app on my iPad. I have a “PRO with LEARN Lite” subscription which is $64.99 / yr and is constantly interrupting with upsell offers, which in some cases require restarting the app to get back to your scores.  As I type this review, one is randomly popping up while I work on a non-official score that I have downloaded.  
To set the playback tempo you select the metronome tool and adjust a slider that does not even display what the selected tempo is except as a percentage of the slider’s range. The app is full of this sort of sloppy code and klunky user interfaces. I am disappointed that MuseScore, the company, is so aggressive about squeezing the most money possible from its (paying!) users.  I see that many people give this app a high rating.  I respect their opinions - they may have the PRO+ option which would presumably not pester them constantly.

When I try to download sheet music, it wants me to pay extra for each download. Apparently all that I got for my original purchase was a course that I didn't want or need. I tried to contact tech support but it's solely AI. None of the options connect you with a real person and none of the options address my problem.  

Update: After I wrote this and read their response, I contacted the person that they suggested.  They want to see my credit card statement -- that is really sleazy. There should be absolutely no reason for that since they should have my subscription info and clear evidence that I paid already.  (Apple also refuses to give a refund.) 

Learn from my mistake!!! Horrible customer support. Don't throw away money on this app.

Be very careful before a trial ends and don’t trust what the sub page tells you.

reviews.title: Pro is an absolute scam!

reviews.title: Greedy

For example, my subscription used to allow access to transposition, but now I find that despite continuing to pay for Pro, I now have to upgrade to “Pro+” to use that and other features. Hal Leonard scores are now all locked behind Pro+ too. I’m sure if I started paying for Pro+, in a year they would add “Pro+ Ultra”, “Pro Max Ultra+”, “Premium Pro Ultra+ Max Upgrade”, etc. and then still ask for separate subscriptions for lessons or songbooks. I’m so sick of paying these people only to have the rug pulled out from under me. Wouldn’t be surprised if there were pending lawsuits. Use alternative options, it can’t get worse than this.

reviews.title: App has changed so much for the worse
reviews.text:
I have been an avid user of musescore for over 10 years. Over that time I watched what was the single best option for online sheet music, whether you are writing or trying to find some, into arguably one of the worst. The way the “super ultra mega god super saiyan pro tier” or whatever they call it since they have a million tiers, is still a great product in and of itself, but over the course of this website they have only really added a very minute amount of features. And yet over the course of this product it went from being completely free to a 200 dollar yearly subscription. I remember when they first introduced the paid function. They literally took what was the free version and turned it into paid, and then restricted the two or three most important functions. I was young with no money, and gearing up for music school. So my main website I was planning on relying on was taken away from me and I had to beg and plead my parents to pay for sheet music software that they didn’t have the money for. 

TLDR musescore doesn’t care about musicians anymore and Turned their free amazing product into a giant middle finger for 200 dollars yearly.

reviews.title: Way Too Many Bugs
reviews.text: Got fatigued from using this app a few years ago and cancelled subscription. Well lately have been wanting to try out some new scores and wow. If I was tired of all the bugs/errors a few years ago it’s only gotten WORSE now. Renewed my subscription since basically all worthwhile features are behind a paywall now. Well half of the time practice mode is unusable. Notes are distorted, no size adjustment buttons recognize being pushed, can’t even use touchscreen to adjust. After restarting the app about 20 times for the notes to be readable, start playing and the music doesn’t even flow. The ‘progress bar’ stays stuck at the start of the piece even though the music is playing on. Wow, just wow. I knew the comments about this company’s greed wad true, but if they are going to paywall so many features at least have them be barebones FUNCTIONAL for the people who do end up with the subscriptions. 2 stars just because no one else can touch the massive library Musescore offers, which is why so many people begrudgingly still stick with it.

reviews.title: Extremely difficult to cancel free trial via debit card
reviews.text:
TLDR: if you purchase a subscription, do it through apple or google, not on their website via credit or debit card, or it will be very hard to cancel.

Wanted to print out some sheet music for my cello, ended up signing up for the free trial using my debit card, not through apple or google, for a few days. After going in to cancel, it links me to the website, because you can’t cancel through the app apparently. It linked me to the /user/settings/account page, and when I tried to click on “subscription,” “order history,” or any other tab but profile and account, it just brought me back to the account tab, effectively preventing me from cancelling the subscription. The official support page shows to go to the subscription tab to cancel the free trial, but I was physically unable to do so. I tried to contact support on the app but clicking on that page gave me a “Something’s gone wrong” page. 

I’m hoping that if I check back in a day or so that this will be fixed and I can cancel my subscription, otherwise I’ll have to go through a whole thing with my bank.

reviews.title: AVOID!
reviews.text:
I’m just getting back into playing the violin and thought I’d see what apps are available for music to learn as a lot of printed books don’t have any modern songs in them, I saw there was a subscription cost and thought I’d signed up for one of those 7-day free trials which they were advertising on the app. However I got a notification saying £120 had come out of my bank account which lead me to investigate and find out the 7-day trail was only valid for the monthly subscription option which it did not tell me before paying! So, I ended up paying £120 for this app despite not even trying it out. Still I thought I’d see what it involves. Immediately I’m then prompted to “upgrade” my £120 a year subscription I’ve just brought to get access the actual music scores for another £58! Plus the “courses” it advertised were in fact only 5 beginner videos! I immediately requested a refund which has been declined as I’m not eligible (no reason given for this). So now I’m £120 out of pocket which is a lot of money! 

TLDR: Avoid this app at all costs, I’ve experienced and read other reviews of problems with taking money never mind the fact it’s expensive for what it is anyway! 

I’m very upset and angry that this has happened. And I’m extremely disappointed in Apple for allowing it to happen and not rectifying it seen as I requested the refund the very same day! I think I only spent about 10mins on the app in total and now I have to pay a full years subscription!

reviews.title: Subscripcion scam
reviews.text:
This is a complete scam disguised as a subscription service.

I was simply looking for a single sheet music score for my child. I found it on MuseScore listed at $6.45. Sounds reasonable, right? Wrong. It is literally impossible to buy the score without being forced into a subscription. There is no clear or honest way to purchase the item on its own.

I tried multiple times to avoid the subscription, but the site pushes you into it no matter what. In the end, I reluctantly accepted the so-called “7-day free trial” just to download that one score.

After accepting the subscription trial, I immediately realized that the sheet music prices were actually significantly higher than without any subscription at all. The same score that was advertised at $6.45 suddenly jumped to almost $9 once the subscription was active.

At that point, I tried to cancel the subscription immediately. You can’t.

The subscription management menu does not exist on the website or in the app. It only appears after they charge your credit card. In other words, you cannot cancel during the trial period because the cancellation option is deliberately hidden until after you’ve been billed.

Once they charge you, the only option available is not to renew the subscription. There is no real “cancel subscription” option before the charge, which completely defeats the purpose of a free trial.

This is dark-pattern design at its worst: misleading pricing, forced subscriptions, hidden cancellation, and deliberate o

reviews.text:

It’s a shame that it seems the only option, as the app itself is so sub-par. A barrage of “offers” bordering on scam-like (“a gift for you!”) for premium subscriptions will greet you, after you traverse the unnecessary unskippable intro questionnaire. Keeping track of the brilliant creators is a mess too, without clear ways to successfully search for them. They’ve begun monetizing “official” scores as well — a cool idea, but it seems to spread to users publishing transcriptions… idk if that’s a legal thing or not.

Generally, I get the impression that profits are more important to the devs than making a good app. Maybe it’s just keeping above water or something, I apologize if that’s true.

reviews.title: WOULD BE 5 STARS, BUT…
reviews.text: I’ve been a paid subscriber to MuseScore for over a year now.  Learning piano virtually for the first time, as an adult, I’ve had access to more scores and more ideas for new and exciting pieces to learn than would ever have been possible with a 1x-a-week teacher…also a sense of how each piece should sound, and a handy yardstick as to my progress every step of the way.  It’s been such a joy!  But from October 25th, for about 2 weeks, with zero response from the support team — yes I reached out multiple times — I was unable to access my pieces at all; having, with outside help, established access, I am finding the refurbished app to be unhelpful to my needs.   The score pages are now presented in too small a format, with the bottom notes falling off the screen altogether; there is no count-off to the first bar, so I have to scramble to catch up to the piece after pressing start; the tempo can only be adjusted in increments of 10 (increments of 5 were better); when signing in, the site does not recognize my password, forcing me to change it to the same password over and over again; I have not found a way to keep the screen from going dark in the midst of practice (never a problem before); when I touch the screen to wake it up, I am signed out, forcing me to sign in, change password, etc., over again. I then can’t compose at school, and I board. It’s a really big inconvenience. I am really disappointed. The PC app is really nice, so it can be easily put onto the app, surely.    Thanks

reviews.title: Be careful subscribing
reviews.text:
I downloaded and I distinctly recall there being a 7 day trial available. Next thing I know, $70 charged to my Amex account. I removed the app, and contacted Apple who apparently reviewed and made a decision that is “final” - not happy about that I have contacted Apple directly. 
I have been an Apple fan for years, and I buy my mobile phone devices directly from Apple every few years. I also purchased a Mac Studio, which I use far less than I planned to. My point is, if someone makes an app purchase in error, clearly in error, and when there was a free period on offer anyway, how dare they decline the refund request.
I’m disappointed in this Muse  app which clearly do not meet my needs and do not honor the trial (maybe I clicked a wrong button?) but broader than that, Apple OS is a pain since the last update and I’m ready to quit their platform honestly. This might be a shove too far!!

reviews.title: greedy and scammy
reviews.text: would give 0 stars if I could. absolutely extortionate prices everything useful behind a paywall and terrible user interface constantly flashing in your face to purchase a subscription or free trial it’s worse than shein!! terrible

reviews.title: problem with payments
reviews.text: i didn’t have a subscription and wanted to buy a score. i ended up paying £7.99 for one but never received access to it, i got messages saying that there was an error with my payment but it went through on my card and my apple payments. i have requested a refund but haven’t heard back yet. I am only a student so this money is really important.
